document.title: Design Element Register and Requirement Allocation

TOOL-AIF-010.text: All AI-assisted features shall be optional; the tool shall provide its full non-AI functionality with AI disabled, and AI shall be disabled by default.

TOOL-AIF-020.text: The tool shall support a locally-executed model requiring no network access.

TOOL-AIF-030.text: The tool shall not transmit user source code, test data, or project metadata to any external service unless the user has explicitly enabled a remote provider for that session.

TOOL-AIF-040.text: The tool shall display, before first use of a remote provider, exactly what data will be transmitted and to whom.

TOOL-AIF-050.text: The tool shall abstract AI providers behind a single interface supporting local runtimes and remote APIs interchangeably.

TOOL-AIF-060.text: The tool shall support AI-assisted generation of test cases targeting specified uncovered code.

TOOL-AIF-070.text: Every AI-generated artifact shall be compiled and executed before presentation; artifacts that fail to compile, crash, or fail to increase coverage shall be discarded or presented as rejected.

TOOL-AIF-080.text: Every AI-generated artifact shall be permanently and visibly marked as AI-generated, including the model identifier and generation timestamp, in the artifact and in all reports.

TOOL-AIF-090.text: AI-generated artifacts shall be recorded as unreviewed until explicitly marked reviewed by an identified user, and reports shall distinguish reviewed from unreviewed.

TOOL-AIF-100.text: The tool shall support a configuration mode that prohibits AI-generated artifacts from contributing to certification evidence.

TOOL-AIF-110.text: The tool shall support AI-assisted generation of stub bodies from calling context.

TOOL-AIF-120.text: The tool shall support AI-assisted explanation of test failures in natural language.

TOOL-AIF-130.text: The tool shall support AI-assisted proposal of links between requirements text and test cases, presented as suggestions requiring confirmation.

TOOL-AIF-140.text: The tool shall support AI-assisted naming and documentation of generated test cases.

TOOL-AIF-150.text: AI operations shall be bounded by configurable time and token limits and shall fail without blocking the surrounding workflow.

TOOL-AIF-160.text: The tool shall record the prompt, model, and parameters used for each AI-generated artifact, for auditability.

TOOL-AIF-170.text: The tool shall document the minimum hardware required for each supported local model configuration.

TOOL-AIF-180.text: AI generation parameters affecting output variability, including sampling temperature and random seed, shall be user-configurable and recorded with each generated artifact.

TOOL-AIF-190.text: The tool shall record the identity and version of the model used to produce each artifact, in a form that remains meaningful after the model is superseded.

TOOL-AIF-200.text: The tool shall verify the integrity of a locally installed model against a published hash before use.

TOOL-AIF-210.text: Where an AI-generated artifact is rejected by the validation required in TOOL-AIF-070, the tool shall record that a rejection occurred, so that acceptance rates are visible rather than hidden.

TOOL-ATG-010.text: The tool shall automatically generate test cases intended to maximize structural coverage of a designated function.

TOOL-ATG-020.text: The tool shall support automatic test vector generation via symbolic execution of the UUT.

TOOL-ATG-030.text: The tool shall support automatic test vector generation via bounded model checking as an alternative or complementary engine.

TOOL-ATG-040.text: Every automatically generated test case shall be emitted in the same format as a manually authored test case and shall be editable thereafter.

TOOL-ATG-050.text: Every automatically generated test case shall be compiled and executed before being presented to the user; test cases that fail to compile or crash the harness shall not be presented as valid.

TOOL-ATG-060.text: The tool shall report, per generation run: number of test cases generated, coverage achieved, and the specific code constructs left uncovered.

TOOL-ATG-070.text: Automatically generated test cases shall be clearly marked as machine-generated in both the artifact and all reports.

TOOL-ATG-080.text: Generated test cases shall record the observed behavior as the expected value, and shall mark that expected value as unreviewed until a user confirms it.

TOOL-ATG-090.text: The tool shall support targeted generation against a specified uncovered line, branch, or condition, rather than whole-function generation only.

TOOL-ATG-100.text: The tool shall bound generation effort by configurable time and memory limits and shall terminate gracefully, returning whatever was generated.

TOOL-ATG-110.text: The tool shall report constructs the generation engine cannot handle (e.g. dynamic memory, floating point, concurrency, inline assembly) rather than failing silently.

TOOL-CBT-010.text: The tool shall re-execute an existing test suite without regeneration or manual reconfiguration.

TOOL-CBT-020.text: The tool shall determine, from a source change, the set of test cases whose covered code was affected.

TOOL-CBT-030.text: The tool shall support executing only the affected subset identified under TOOL-CBT-020.

TOOL-CBT-040.text: When a subset is executed, all reports shall state clearly that the run was partial and identify which tests were not executed.

TOOL-CBT-050.text: The tool shall compare a test run against a previous run and report newly failing, newly passing, and newly added tests.

TOOL-CBT-060.text: The tool shall report coverage change relative to a baseline run.

TOOL-CBT-070.text: The tool shall detect that a test case is stale because the interface it exercises has changed.

TOOL-CBT-080.text: The tool shall support test suite minimization, identifying redundant test cases contributing no unique coverage.

TOOL-CIC-010.text: All tool functionality required for automated verification shall be accessible from a non-interactive command-line interface.

TOOL-CIC-020.text: The tool shall operate without a graphical environment or display server.

TOOL-CIC-030.text: The tool shall use documented, stable exit codes distinguishing: success, test failure, coverage threshold failure, and tool error.

TOOL-CIC-040.text: The tool shall be installable and executable within a container image.

TOOL-CIC-050.text: The project shall provide reference pipeline configurations for GitHub Actions and GitLab CI.

TOOL-CIC-060.text: The tool shall support sharding a test suite across multiple CI runners and merging the resulting reports.

TOOL-CIC-070.text: The tool shall support caching of ingestion and analysis artifacts across CI runs.

TOOL-CIC-080.text: All tool configuration shall be expressible in version-controlled files; no configuration shall exist only in a GUI or local state.

TOOL-COV-010.text: The tool shall measure statement coverage.

TOOL-COV-020.text: The tool shall measure branch/decision coverage.

TOOL-COV-030.text: The tool shall measure function coverage.

TOOL-COV-040.text: The tool shall measure function call coverage.

TOOL-COV-050.text: The tool shall measure Modified Condition/Decision Coverage (MC/DC).

TOOL-COV-060.text: The tool shall state explicitly, in the user documentation and in every report, which MC/DC form is measured (masking or unique-cause) and by which compiler mechanism.

TOOL-COV-070.text: The tool shall report, for each partially covered decision, which individual conditions were not exercised true and which were not exercised false.

TOOL-COV-080.text: The tool shall detect and report boolean expressions that the compiler could not instrument for MC/DC, including those exceeding compiler condition-count limits.

TOOL-COV-090.text: The tool shall support unique-cause MC/DC, or shall document the precise gap between the supported form and unique-cause MC/DC.

TOOL-COV-100.text: The tool shall retrieve coverage data from bare-metal targets with no filesystem and no operating system.

TOOL-COV-110.text: The tool shall merge coverage data across multiple test executions into a single result set.

TOOL-COV-120.text: The tool shall attribute coverage to individual test cases, enabling per-test coverage reporting.

TOOL-COV-130.text: The tool shall enforce configurable minimum coverage thresholds per metric and fail the run when they are not met.

TOOL-COV-140.text: The tool shall support coverage-by-analysis: recording a user-supplied justification for code that cannot be covered by test, and reflecting it in reports as justified rather than covered.

TOOL-COV-150.text: Justifications under TOOL-COV-140 shall record author, date, and rationale, and shall be invalidated when the associated source changes.

TOOL-COV-160.text: The tool shall report coverage of the unit under test separately from coverage of harness, stub, and framework code.

TOOL-COV-170.text: The tool shall support control coupling and data coupling analysis between integrated units.

TOOL-EXE-010.text: The tool shall build and execute the test harness on the development host.

TOOL-EXE-020.text: The tool shall report, per test case: pass, fail, or error, with failures identifying the assertion, expected value, actual value, and source location.

TOOL-EXE-030.text: The tool shall isolate test execution such that a crash, hang, or abort in one test case does not prevent the remaining test cases from executing.

TOOL-EXE-040.text: The tool shall enforce a configurable per-test timeout and report timed-out tests as failures.

TOOL-EXE-050.text: The tool shall execute independent test executables in parallel, with configurable concurrency.

TOOL-EXE-060.text: The tool shall return a non-zero process exit status when any test fails, for CI consumption.

TOOL-EXE-070.text: The tool shall support launching a test case under a debugger, with the harness prepared and execution stopped at entry to the function under test.

TOOL-EXE-080.text: The tool shall support incremental rebuild, recompiling only artifacts affected by a change.

TOOL-EXE-090.text: The tool shall detect and report memory errors during host execution via sanitizer integration, without such detection being mandatory.

TOOL-HAR-010.text: The tool shall generate a compilable test harness for a designated unit under test (UUT) from the analysis model, without manual editing.

TOOL-HAR-020.text: The generated harness shall expose every non-static function of the UUT as directly callable from test code.

TOOL-HAR-030.text: The generated harness shall optionally expose `static` functions of the UUT for testing.

TOOL-HAR-040.text: The generated harness shall provide read and write access to global and file-static variables identified by TOOL-PAR-050.

TOOL-HAR-050.text: The generated harness shall include per-test setup and teardown hooks.

TOOL-HAR-060.text: The tool shall generate harnesses targeting a configurable test framework back-end, supporting at minimum Unity and cmocka. Neither back-end shall introduce a C++ compilation or runtime dependency.

TOOL-HAR-065.text: The tool shall provide an optional GoogleTest back-end for host-only execution, for interoperability with existing GoogleTest suites and tooling. This back-end shall not be required for any documented workflow.

TOOL-HAR-070.text: Harness generation shall be template-driven such that support for an additional test framework requires only new templates, not tool source changes.

TOOL-HAR-080.text: The tool shall generate an integration-level harness spanning two or more units, stubbing only dependencies external to the selected set.

TOOL-HAR-090.text: Generated harness code shall be human-readable, deterministically formatted, and carry a header identifying it as generated, the generating tool version, and the source model.

TOOL-HAR-100.text: Regenerating a harness shall preserve user modifications in designated user-editable regions, or shall detect and report conflicts rather than silently overwriting.

TOOL-HAR-110.text: The tool shall detect and report when the UUT interface has changed such that an existing harness is stale.

TOOL-HAR-120.text: The tool shall resolve all undefined external references in the harness link step, either by stub generation or by explicit user-supplied linkage, and shall report any that remain unresolved.

TOOL-ING-010.text: The tool shall accept a JSON compilation database (`compile_commands.json`) as the primary description of a user's project.

TOOL-ING-020.text: The tool shall parse both the `command` (string) and `arguments` (array) forms of compilation database entries and normalize them internally.

TOOL-ING-030.text: The tool shall extract, per translation unit: source path, working directory, include paths, preprocessor definitions, language standard, and compiler invocation.

TOOL-ING-040.text: The tool shall document and support generating a compilation database via CMake (`CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS`) as the recommended path.

TOOL-ING-050.text: The tool shall support generating a compilation database via build interception (e.g. Bear) for projects without native export.

TOOL-ING-060.text: The tool shall operate on a single `.c` file with user-supplied include paths and defines when no build system is available.

TOOL-ING-070.text: The tool shall detect and report ingestion failures — missing headers, unresolvable include paths, unknown compiler flags — with the offending file and flag identified.

TOOL-ING-080.text: The tool shall import project configuration from Keil uVision (`.uvprojx`), IAR EW (`.ewp`), and Eclipse/STM32CubeIDE project files.

TOOL-ING-090.text: The tool shall persist the ingested project model to a version-controllable text format so ingestion need not be repeated on every invocation.

TOOL-ING-100.text: The tool shall detect that the ingested project model is stale relative to the build system and re-ingest or warn.

TOOL-ING-110.text: The tool shall support ingestion of projects that build with more than one toolchain, retaining per-toolchain flags.

TOOL-ING-120.text: The tool shall accept a set of two or more C source files as a single ingestion scope, for the purpose of integration testing, without requiring a build system.

TOOL-ING-130.text: The tool shall support a named **test scope** as a first-class concept: a user-defined set of translation units treated as the code under test, with all dependencies outside the set treated as external.

TOOL-ING-140.text: For a test scope containing multiple translation units, the tool shall resolve inter-file dependencies internally to the scope and classify each function call as intra-scope or external.

TOOL-ING-150.text: The tool shall support a test scope defined by explicit file list, by directory, by glob pattern, and by build-system target.

TOOL-ING-160.text: The tool shall detect and report symbol conflicts within a test scope, including duplicate non-static definitions and colliding file-static identifiers.

TOOL-ING-170.text: The tool shall support a single translation unit belonging to more than one test scope, such that a file may be tested in isolation and again as part of an integration scope.

TOOL-ING-180.text: The tool shall report, for a given test scope, the complete list of external dependencies requiring stubs, before harness generation is performed.

TOOL-ING-190.text: Test scope definitions shall be stored in a plain-text, version-controllable file.

TOOL-INS-010.text: The tool shall provide a fully offline installation path requiring no network access at install time.

TOOL-INS-020.text: The tool shall be installable without administrative privileges.

TOOL-INS-030.text: Installation shall not require the user to install or configure a language runtime, package manager, or compiler beyond their existing C toolchain.

TOOL-INS-040.text: Each release shall be archivable as a self-contained artifact that can be retained and reinstalled years later without reference to any external service.

TOOL-INS-050.text: Multiple versions of the tool shall be installable side by side, so that a project can remain pinned to the version under which its evidence was produced.

TOOL-INS-060.text: Upgrading shall not modify or migrate existing project data without explicit user confirmation.

TOOL-INS-070.text: The tool shall provide a documented uninstallation procedure that removes all installed components and identifies any user data left in place.

TOOL-INS-080.text: On first run the tool shall verify its environment — toolchain presence, versions, and feature availability — and report clearly what is missing or unsupported.

TOOL-INS-090.text: The tool shall provide a container image suitable for CI use, versioned in lockstep with releases.

TOOL-INS-100.text: The tool shall support a shared network or read-only installation serving multiple users, with per-user state held separately.

TOOL-INS-110.text: The tool shall report its version, build identifier, and the versions of its principal dependencies on request.

TOOL-LIC-010.text: The tool's own source code shall be released under a permissive open-source license.

TOOL-LIC-020.text: Components under strong copyleft licenses shall be invoked as separate processes and shall not be linked into the tool.

TOOL-LIC-030.text: The project shall maintain a Software Bill of Materials listing every dependency, its version, and its license.

TOOL-LIC-040.text: Code generated by the tool shall be free of licensing restriction imposed by the tool, and this shall be stated explicitly in the documentation.

TOOL-LIC-050.text: The tool shall not bundle any component whose license prohibits commercial use or redistribution.

TOOL-LIC-060.text: The build shall verify dependency licenses automatically and fail on introduction of a disallowed license.

TOOL-LIC-070.text: Optional components with restrictive licenses shall be separable, such that a build excluding them remains fully functional for its documented feature set.

TOOL-MIG-010.text: The tool shall execute existing test suites written against supported frameworks (Unity, cmocka) without requiring them to be rewritten.

TOOL-MIG-020.text: The tool shall import an existing Ceedling project, preserving test cases and configuration.

TOOL-MIG-030.text: The tool shall import test case data from commercial tools where those tools provide a documented or plain-text export format, converting inputs, expected values, and stub configuration.

TOOL-MIG-040.text: Import shall report, per imported artifact, what was converted, what was converted with loss of fidelity, and what could not be converted, rather than silently discarding content.

TOOL-MIG-050.text: The tool shall import test cases from a documented CSV interchange format, permitting migration via spreadsheet from any source.

TOOL-MIG-060.text: The tool shall export test cases and results in documented open formats sufficient to reconstruct them in another tool, so that adopting this tool does not create lock-in.

TOOL-MIG-070.text: The tool shall support coexistence: operating on a project that is also tested by another tool, without interfering with that tool's artifacts.

TOOL-MIG-080.text: The tool shall import and export coverage data in standard interchange formats, permitting aggregation with coverage produced by other tools.

TOOL-MIG-090.text: The tool shall provide a migration assessment mode that analyses an existing project and reports the expected fidelity and manual effort of migration before migration is attempted.

TOOL-MIG-100.text: All interchange formats the tool consumes or produces shall be documented to a level permitting independent implementation.

TOOL-NFR-010.text: The tool shall run on Linux x86-64.

TOOL-NFR-020.text: The tool shall run on Windows and macOS.

TOOL-NFR-030.text: Environment creation for a single translation unit of 1000 lines shall complete in under 30 seconds on typical developer hardware.

TOOL-NFR-040.text: Incremental re-execution of an unchanged test suite of 100 test cases shall complete in under 10 seconds on host.

TOOL-NFR-050.text: The tool shall scale to projects of at least 500 translation units and 10,000 test cases.

TOOL-NFR-060.text: All tool outputs shall be deterministic and reproducible given identical inputs.

TOOL-NFR-070.text: The tool shall not modify user source files.

TOOL-NFR-080.text: All tool-generated files shall be written to a designated output directory, separable from user source.

TOOL-NFR-090.text: The tool shall fail safely: on internal error it shall report the error and exit non-zero rather than emitting incomplete or misleading results.

TOOL-NFR-100.text: The tool shall not require network access for any non-AI functionality.

TOOL-NFR-110.text: Installation shall not require administrative privileges.

TOOL-NFR-120.text: The tool shall provide user documentation covering installation, every supported workflow, and every configuration option.

TOOL-NFR-130.text: The tool shall log its operations at configurable verbosity to support diagnosis of failures.

TOOL-NFR-140.text: The tool's own test suite shall achieve and maintain a documented coverage threshold of its own source.

TOOL-NFR-150.text: The tool shall operate within a documented memory ceiling on a project of the scale defined in TOOL-NFR-050, and shall degrade predictably rather than exhausting host memory.

TOOL-NFR-160.text: The tool shall produce, on request, a diagnostic bundle containing version information, configuration, and logs sufficient to reproduce a reported defect, with its contents documented per TOOL-SEC-120.

TOOL-NFR-170.text: The tool shall be used to test the C components of its own implementation, where such components exist.

TOOL-NFR-180.text: Long-running operations shall be interruptible, and interruption shall leave project data in a valid state.

TOOL-NFR-190.text: User-facing text shall be externalized from code to permit translation, without translation being delivered in v1.0.

TOOL-PAR-010.text: The tool shall parse C source using a production C front-end (libclang) with the exact flags recorded in the compilation database.

TOOL-PAR-020.text: The tool shall support C89, C99, C11, C17, and GNU dialect extensions.

TOOL-PAR-030.text: The tool shall extract, for every function in a translation unit: name, return type, parameter names and types, storage class, linkage, and source location.

TOOL-PAR-040.text: The tool shall extract all user-defined types (struct, union, enum, typedef, function pointer) reachable from a function's interface, transitively.

TOOL-PAR-050.text: The tool shall identify global and file-static variables read or written by each function.

TOOL-PAR-060.text: The tool shall construct a call graph identifying, for each function, all functions it calls, and classify each callee as internal (defined in the unit under test) or external.

TOOL-PAR-070.text: The tool shall construct a control flow graph per function sufficient to support coverage analysis and test generation.

TOOL-PAR-080.text: The tool shall identify `static` functions and provide a mechanism to make them testable without modifying user source.

TOOL-PAR-090.text: The tool shall resolve function-like and object-like macros used in interfaces, and record where a macro obscures the true interface.

TOOL-PAR-100.text: The tool shall persist the analysis result as a machine-readable model (JSON) that is the sole input to downstream generation stages.

TOOL-PAR-110.text: The analysis model shall be versioned, with a schema version field, so downstream stages can reject incompatible models.

TOOL-PAR-120.text: The tool shall compute cyclomatic complexity per function and expose it in the model.

TOOL-PAR-130.text: The tool shall continue analysis and report partial results when a subset of translation units fails to parse.

TOOL-PLG-010.text: The tool shall define documented extension points for, at minimum: compiler configurations, test framework back-ends, target execution methods, and report formats.

TOOL-PLG-020.text: Adding a compiler configuration shall require only a declarative configuration file, with no modification of tool source.

TOOL-PLG-030.text: Adding a test framework back-end shall require only new templates and a declarative descriptor, with no modification of tool source.

TOOL-PLG-040.text: Adding a target execution method shall be possible through a documented interface and a user-supplied script.

TOOL-PLG-050.text: Adding a report format shall be possible by consuming the documented intermediate report model, without re-executing tests.

TOOL-PLG-060.text: Extension interfaces shall be versioned, and breaking changes shall be documented with a migration path.

TOOL-PLG-070.text: The tool shall discover and load user-supplied extensions from a documented location without requiring reinstallation.

TOOL-PLG-080.text: The tool shall report clearly when an extension fails to load or is incompatible, and shall continue operating with the remaining functionality.

TOOL-PLG-090.text: The tool's own built-in compiler configurations, framework back-ends, and report formats shall be implemented through the same public extension points available to users, so those interfaces are proven by use.

TOOL-PRJ-010.text: All project data shall be stored in documented, plain-text, human-readable formats.

TOOL-PRJ-020.text: Every project data file shall carry an explicit schema version.

TOOL-PRJ-030.text: The tool shall open projects created by earlier versions, or shall report precisely why it cannot and what migration is required.

TOOL-PRJ-040.text: Project data migration shall be explicit, reversible where possible, and shall never occur without user confirmation.

TOOL-PRJ-050.text: Project data shall be stable under version control: operations that do not change meaning shall not change file content, and file ordering shall be deterministic.

TOOL-PRJ-060.text: Project data shall be structured such that concurrent edits by multiple users produce localized, resolvable version control conflicts rather than whole-file conflicts.

TOOL-PRJ-070.text: Project data shall reference user source by relative path, so that a project remains valid when the working tree is relocated or cloned.

TOOL-PRJ-080.text: Generated artifacts shall be distinguishable from user-authored artifacts by location or explicit marking, so that generated content can be excluded from version control.

TOOL-PRJ-090.text: The tool shall detect and report when project data references source, requirements, or configuration that no longer exists.

TOOL-PRJ-100.text: The tool shall support exporting a complete, self-contained record of a verification run — configuration, test cases, results, coverage, and tool version — suitable for long-term archival.

TOOL-PRJ-110.text: The tool shall support verifying an archived record against the tool version that produced it, reporting whether the record can be reproduced.

TOOL-QUA-010.text: The tool shall be accompanied by a Tool Classification analysis addressing ISO 26262-8 Tool Impact and Tool error Detection, yielding a Tool Confidence Level.

TOOL-QUA-020.text: The tool shall be accompanied by a documented Tool Operational Requirements specification defining its intended use, operating environment, and known limitations.

TOOL-QUA-030.text: The tool shall have a validation test suite demonstrating that it satisfies its Tool Operational Requirements, executable by the end user.

TOOL-QUA-040.text: The tool shall publish a documented list of known errors and their workarounds, maintained per release.

TOOL-QUA-050.text: Each release shall be uniquely identified and archived such that a specific version can be reproduced.

TOOL-QUA-060.text: The tool shall record, in every artifact it generates, sufficient information to reproduce that artifact.

TOOL-QUA-070.text: The tool shall document its own development process, change control, and defect management to support user assessment.

TOOL-QUA-080.text: The tool shall document the mapping between its capabilities and the verification objectives of ISO 26262, IEC 61508, IEC 62304, EN 50128, and DO-178C.

TOOL-QUA-090.text: The tool shall not claim certification or qualification it does not hold; documentation shall state clearly what qualification evidence is provided and what remains the user's responsibility.

TOOL-QUA-100.text: The tool shall provide templates for the user's own tool qualification artifacts.

TOOL-REP-010.text: The tool shall produce a machine-readable test result report in JUnit XML format.

TOOL-REP-020.text: The tool shall produce a machine-readable coverage report in a standard format (Cobertura XML and/or LCOV).

TOOL-REP-030.text: The tool shall produce a human-readable HTML report combining test results and coverage.

TOOL-REP-040.text: The HTML report shall present annotated source code showing per-line coverage status.

TOOL-REP-050.text: The HTML report shall present, for each decision, the MC/DC condition status detail required by TOOL-COV-070.

TOOL-REP-060.text: The tool shall produce a verification report suitable for submission as certification evidence, containing: tool identification and version, configuration, test cases executed with results, coverage achieved per metric, justified exclusions, and the traceability matrix.

TOOL-REP-070.text: Every report shall record the tool version, the compiler and version used, the target executed on, and the timestamp of execution.

TOOL-REP-080.text: The tool shall produce reports in a paginated, archivable format (PDF) for records retention.

TOOL-REP-090.text: All report formats shall be generated from a single documented intermediate data model, so custom report formats can be added without re-running tests.

TOOL-REP-100.text: Report generation shall be deterministic: identical inputs shall produce byte-identical reports, excluding timestamps.

TOOL-REP-110.text: The tool shall produce a summary report aggregating results across multiple units, targets, and toolchains.

TOOL-REP-120.text: The tool shall report coverage trend across successive runs.

TOOL-REP-130.text: Report formats used as certification evidence shall be versioned, and changes to them shall be documented, so that archived reports remain interpretable.

TOOL-REP-140.text: Every report shall identify the test scope it covers and shall state explicitly what was excluded from that scope.

TOOL-REP-150.text: The tool shall support generating a report from previously archived result data without re-executing tests.

TOOL-SEC-010.text: Every release artifact shall be cryptographically signed, and the signature verification procedure shall be documented.

TOOL-SEC-020.text: Every release shall publish a Software Bill of Materials with the resolved version and cryptographic hash of every dependency.

TOOL-SEC-030.text: The build shall be reproducible: an independent party building from a given source revision shall obtain functionally identical artifacts, and the procedure shall be documented.

TOOL-SEC-040.text: Dependencies shall be pinned to exact versions with integrity hashes; the build shall fail on hash mismatch.

TOOL-SEC-050.text: The tool shall warn before executing user-supplied code — including test cases, stub bodies, and build scripts — from a project the user has not previously opened.

TOOL-SEC-060.text: The tool shall support executing test harnesses under a restricted execution context limiting filesystem and network access, without such restriction being mandatory.

TOOL-SEC-070.text: The tool shall not execute code embedded in project configuration files. Configuration shall be data, not script.

TOOL-SEC-080.text: The project shall document a security disclosure process and a supported-version policy.

TOOL-SEC-090.text: Where the tool retrieves data from a target device or external process, it shall treat that data as untrusted input and shall not execute or interpret it as code.

TOOL-SEC-100.text: The project shall perform automated dependency vulnerability scanning as part of its own CI, and shall publish the results.

TOOL-SEC-110.text: Credentials, tokens, and API keys for optional remote services shall be stored using platform-provided secure storage and shall never be written to project files, logs, or reports.

TOOL-SEC-120.text: Diagnostic output and logs shall not contain user source code content beyond what is necessary to identify a location, and the tool shall document exactly what a diagnostic bundle contains.

TOOL-STB-010.text: The tool shall automatically generate a stub for every external function called by the UUT.

TOOL-STB-020.text: Each generated stub shall have a signature identical to the function it replaces.

TOOL-STB-030.text: The tool shall generate, per stub, the type and structure declarations required for the stub to compile independently.

TOOL-STB-040.text: Generated stubs shall support, per test case: a configured return value, a sequence of return values across successive calls, and a user-supplied callback implementation.

TOOL-STB-050.text: Generated stubs shall record call count, and the argument values of each call, retrievable from test code.

TOOL-STB-060.text: Generated stubs shall support verification of call order across multiple stubs.

TOOL-STB-070.text: Generated stubs shall support output parameters, writing caller-supplied values through pointer arguments.

TOOL-STB-080.text: The user shall be able to disable stubbing for any individual function, linking the real implementation instead.

TOOL-STB-090.text: The tool shall support intercepting calls made by the UUT to functions defined within the UUT itself (call wrapping), without modifying user source.

TOOL-STB-100.text: The tool shall support stubbing of standard library functions on explicit user request.

TOOL-STB-110.text: Generated stubs shall be user-editable, with editable regions clearly delimited from regenerated regions.

TOOL-STB-120.text: When the source function signature changes, the tool shall re-synchronize the stub signature while preserving the user-authored body where the change permits, and shall report where it does not.

TOOL-STB-130.text: The tool shall flag, in generated output, every construct it could not fully handle (e.g. variadic functions, complex function pointers) using a consistent, greppable marker.

TOOL-STB-140.text: The tool shall support stubbing functions reached through function pointers, including function pointer members of structures.

TOOL-TCD-010.text: The tool shall support test cases authored directly in C source against the generated harness.

TOOL-TCD-020.text: The tool shall support data-driven test cases, in which input values, expected outputs, and stub behavior are specified as data separate from code.

TOOL-TCD-030.text: Data-driven test cases shall be stored in a plain-text, diffable, version-controllable format.

TOOL-TCD-040.text: A test case shall be able to specify: input parameter values, initial values of accessed globals, expected return value, expected final values of globals, expected output parameter values, and stub behavior and expectations.

TOOL-TCD-050.text: The tool shall support expected-value comparison for all scalar C types, enums, pointers, arrays, structs, and unions.

TOOL-TCD-060.text: The tool shall support tolerance-based comparison for floating-point expected values.

TOOL-TCD-070.text: The tool shall support ranged inputs, generating one executed test per value in the range.

TOOL-TCD-080.text: The tool shall support test case grouping into named suites, and selective execution by suite, unit, function, or test name.

TOOL-TCD-090.text: Test cases shall be independent: execution order shall not affect results, and the tool shall support randomized ordering to detect violations.

TOOL-TCD-100.text: The tool shall support import and export of test cases in a documented interchange format (CSV or equivalent).

TOOL-TCD-110.text: The tool shall support test case derivation via boundary value analysis and equivalence class partitioning of input parameters.

TOOL-TCD-120.text: The tool shall support classification-tree-based test case design.

TOOL-TCD-130.text: The tool shall support robustness test cases supplying out-of-range and invalid input values with normal range checking disabled.

TOOL-TCD-140.text: Each test case shall carry a stable unique identifier, preserved across edits and regeneration, for traceability purposes.

TOOL-TCH-010.text: The tool shall support GCC and Clang as host compilers.

TOOL-TCH-020.text: The tool shall define a declarative compiler configuration format specifying: compiler invocation, flag syntax for coverage/debug/optimization, output conventions, and supported coverage kinds.

TOOL-TCH-030.text: The tool shall support cross-compilation using GNU-style embedded toolchains, verified against at minimum `arm-none-eabi-gcc` and a RISC-V GNU toolchain.

TOOL-TCH-040.text: The tool shall support additional cross-compilers via user-authored compiler configuration files without requiring changes to the tool's source code.

TOOL-TCH-050.text: The tool shall ship compiler configurations for at minimum: GCC (host), Clang (host), arm-none-eabi-gcc, riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc, avr-gcc, and SDCC.

TOOL-TCH-060.text: The tool shall declare, per compiler configuration, which coverage metrics are achievable, and shall refuse to request unsupported metrics.

TOOL-TCH-070.text: The tool shall detect the compiler version and reject or warn when the version does not support a requested feature (e.g. MC/DC requiring GCC ≥ 14 or Clang ≥ 18).

TOOL-TCH-080.text: The tool shall support building the same test suite for multiple toolchains in isolated build directories within one invocation.

TOOL-TCH-090.text: The tool shall provide reproducible container images containing validated host and cross toolchains.

TOOL-TCH-100.text: The tool shall support proprietary compilers (Keil armcc/armclang, IAR, TASKING, Green Hills) through the compiler configuration mechanism where their invocation is externally scriptable.

TOOL-TGT-010.text: The tool shall build the test harness for a cross-compiled embedded target.

TOOL-TGT-020.text: The tool shall execute the test harness on an instruction-set simulator, verified against QEMU and Renode.

TOOL-TGT-030.text: The tool shall execute the test harness on physical target hardware via a debug probe.

TOOL-TGT-040.text: The tool shall support flashing target hardware via OpenOCD, pyOCD, and J-Link.

TOOL-TGT-050.text: The tool shall retrieve test results from the target via at minimum: semihosting, and a serial (UART) channel.

TOOL-TGT-060.text: The host-to-target result protocol shall be plain-text, line-oriented, and parseable without requiring a bidirectional channel.

TOOL-TGT-070.text: Test cases shall execute unmodified on host and target, with only configuration distinguishing the two.

TOOL-TGT-080.text: The tool shall support a declarative hardware inventory describing connected targets: identifier, platform, probe type, serial device, and flash timeout.

TOOL-TGT-090.text: The tool shall detect target execution failures — flash failure, no output, target reset, watchdog — and distinguish them from test failures.

TOOL-TGT-100.text: The tool shall support splitting a test suite across multiple target executions when the full suite exceeds target memory.

TOOL-TGT-110.text: The tool shall document the RAM, flash, and stack overhead of the on-target harness, per configuration.

TOOL-TGT-120.text: The tool shall support execution on targets without a debug probe via a user-supplied flashing and communication script.

TOOL-TRC-010.text: The tool shall support associating one or more requirement identifiers with each test case.

TOOL-TRC-020.text: The tool shall generate a bidirectional traceability matrix linking requirements to test cases and test cases to requirements.

TOOL-TRC-030.text: The traceability matrix shall report the pass/fail status of each linked test case.

TOOL-TRC-040.text: The tool shall report requirements with no linked test case, and test cases with no linked requirement.

TOOL-TRC-050.text: The tool shall import requirements from ReqIF.

TOOL-TRC-060.text: The tool shall import requirements from CSV and from a documented plain-text format.

TOOL-TRC-070.text: The tool shall export traceability data in ReqIF for exchange with external requirements management tools.

TOOL-TRC-080.text: The tool shall link requirements to source code elements in addition to test cases.

TOOL-TRC-090.text: The tool shall detect when a requirement has changed since its linked test cases were last executed or reviewed.

TOOL-TRC-100.text: The tool shall interoperate with an established open-source traceability tool rather than requiring its own requirements database.

TOOL-UIX-010.text: The tool's core shall be a command-line engine; all graphical interfaces shall be clients of that engine and shall provide no capability unavailable from it.

TOOL-UIX-020.text: The engine shall expose a documented, versioned interface (JSON over stdio or local socket) for front-end clients.

TOOL-UIX-030.text: The tool shall provide a standalone graphical application that supports the complete test workflow — project creation, environment build, test authoring, execution, coverage review, and reporting — without requiring the installation of any editor, IDE, or third-party host application.

TOOL-UIX-040.text: The standalone application shall be installable and runnable by a user who has no development environment beyond a C toolchain.

TOOL-UIX-050.text: The standalone application shall operate against a local engine instance and shall require no network access.

TOOL-UIX-060.text: The application shall support creating, opening, saving, and closing a test project that references user source without copying or modifying it.

TOOL-UIX-070.text: The application shall provide a guided environment-creation workflow collecting: source selection or test scope, compiler configuration, target (host or embedded), coverage kind, and test framework back-end.

TOOL-UIX-080.text: The application shall support creating an integration test environment by selecting multiple source files into a single test scope, and shall display the resulting internal/external dependency classification before the environment is built.

TOOL-UIX-090.text: The application shall display environment build progress and, on failure, the compiler diagnostics responsible, navigable to the offending source location.

TOOL-UIX-100.text: The application shall support managing multiple environments within one project and executing across a selected subset.

TOOL-UIX-110.text: The application shall present a hierarchical navigation tree: project → environment → unit → function → test case.

TOOL-UIX-120.text: Each tree node shall display aggregated status: pass/fail counts, coverage percentage, and whether the node is stale relative to its source.

TOOL-UIX-130.text: The application shall support selecting any tree node and executing, editing, or reporting on that node's scope.

TOOL-UIX-140.text: The application shall support filtering and searching the tree by name, status, and coverage threshold.

TOOL-UIX-150.text: The application shall provide a tabular editor for data-driven test cases, presenting input parameters, global variables, and expected values as editable fields.

TOOL-UIX-160.text: The test case editor shall present structured and array parameters as an expandable tree, permitting entry of values at any depth.

TOOL-UIX-170.text: The test case editor shall be type-aware, constraining or validating entered values against the declared C type and presenting enumeration constants by name.

TOOL-UIX-180.text: The application shall provide a stub configuration view listing every external dependency of the environment, with per-stub controls to enable or disable stubbing and to define return values, return sequences, and output parameter values.

TOOL-UIX-190.text: The application shall support entering ranged and boundary-derived input values, displaying the resulting number of generated test cases before they are created.

TOOL-UIX-200.text: The application shall provide an editor for test cases authored directly in C, with syntax highlighting, alongside the tabular editor.

TOOL-UIX-210.text: The application shall support executing a selection of tests with visible progress and the ability to cancel a run in progress.

TOOL-UIX-220.text: The application shall present per-test results identifying, for each failure, the assertion, expected value, actual value, and source location, navigable to that location.

TOOL-UIX-230.text: The application shall support launching a test case under a debugger with execution stopped at entry to the function under test.

TOOL-UIX-240.text: The application shall present a console pane displaying the engine commands executed on the user's behalf, so that any GUI action can be reproduced from the command line.

TOOL-UIX-250.text: The application shall present annotated source with per-line coverage status distinguishing covered, uncovered, partially covered, and justified-by-analysis.

TOOL-UIX-260.text: The application shall present, for each partially covered decision, the per-condition detail required by TOOL-COV-070, in a form that identifies which condition outcomes remain unexercised.

TOOL-UIX-270.text: The application shall present a graphical control flow view of a function with coverage status overlaid.

TOOL-UIX-280.text: The application shall present coverage summarized by project, environment, unit, and function, with drill-down between levels.

TOOL-UIX-290.text: The application shall support recording a coverage-by-analysis justification against a specific uncovered construct, capturing author and rationale.

TOOL-UIX-300.text: The application shall support generating and viewing all report formats defined in Section 15 without leaving the application.

TOOL-UIX-310.text: The application shall present the requirements traceability matrix, with navigation from a requirement to its linked test cases and results.

TOOL-UIX-320.text: All project, environment, test case, and configuration state shall be stored in plain-text, version-controllable files. The graphical application shall never be the sole source of any state.

TOOL-UIX-330.text: A project created, modified, or executed through the graphical application shall be fully usable from the command line thereafter, and the reverse.

TOOL-UIX-340.text: The standalone application shall run on Linux x86-64 and Windows x86-64.

TOOL-UIX-350.text: The application shall transmit no telemetry, usage data, or user content to any external service.

TOOL-UIX-360.text: The application shall provide error messages identifying the affected file, line, and a concrete remedy.

TOOL-UIX-370.text: The application shall remain responsive during long-running operations, performing analysis, build, and execution without blocking the interface.

TOOL-UIX-380.text: The application shall support a keyboard-driven workflow for its primary operations.

TOOL-UIX-390.text: Editor and IDE integrations may be provided as additional thin clients of the engine interface defined in TOOL-UIX-020. Such integrations are explicitly out of scope for v1.0 and shall never be a prerequisite for any workflow.

TOOL-UIX-400.text: A browser-based interface for viewing results and coverage across multiple projects may be provided for team-level and CI use. Out of scope for v1.0.
